newsitem.title: GERMANY: German tax talks continuing after three hours.
newsitem.headline: German tax talks continuing after three hours.

text.p: The meeting between Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition government and leaders from the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) on Tuesday to discuss tax reforms was still continuing after three hours.

The length of the meeting led the parliamentary faction of Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU/CSU) to postpone a planned meeting by an hour to 1400 GMT local time. Faction leader Wolfgang Schaeuble was attending the talks.

The SPD and junior coalition partners the Free Democrats (FDP) were meeting as planned, but with stand-ins deputising for SPD parliament chief Rudolf Scharping and the FDP's Hermann Otto Solms, both of whom were at the talks in the chancellery.
Sources who had had access to the talks said they were proving to be difficult.
The talks were seen by both sides as a last chance to strike a compromise deal over Finance Minister Theo Waigel's plan to cut 30 billion marks in income and corporate taxes over the next two years.

The SPD wants a series of Keynesian measures to boost consumer demand -- in addition to cuts in the bottom rate of income tax the SPD wants to cut labour insurance charges, boost child benefits and increasing tax allowances.
